text:
Shane: Heads-up — I sketched a lightweight handoff pattern for preemptible GPU evictions. Goal: keep streaming/generator requests from dropping outputs while minimizing duplicated work and latency spikes. TL;DR: short graceful drain + per-request resume token + brokered requeue with a fast backoff.

Priya: sketch pls, high level first. How short is "short" for drain? and what about token leak risk? :thinking_face:

Shane: High level: when VM signals eviction, runtime marks node DRAINING (SLO window ~10s), flushes KV cache for active sessions to storage, and issues resume tokens to in-flight requests. We let clients continue receiving final bytes; any unfinished requests get a resume token that encodes progress + id. Then a broker (central requeue service) immediately retries the request on another pool) with idempotency guard.

Alex: How do we encode the token? we need it to be small and not leak model state. Suggest: opaque resume pointer that references server-side checkpoint (short-lived) rather than sending large KV. Example token format: ```resume:v1:$node_id:$req_id:$offset:$sig``` where sig = HMAC(kmgmt, payload). Token lifetime TTL=30s.

Priya: okay HMAC is fine. but where do we persist the checkpoint? ephemeral s3 / redis? we need <10ms lookup on requeue path.

Maria: redis with single-key per request sounds ok if we TTL aggressively. Plan: write {node,req,offset,meta} into redis cluster with TTL 30s during drain. Broker will attempt to fetch on requeue; fallback to full replay if not found.

Shane: exact timings I propose: drain window=10s, kv flush start immediately, broker requeue attempt after 50ms, max requeues=3 with exponential backoff base=150ms. This keeps tail latency bounded and avoids huge amplification.

evict-bot: [eviction notice] node gpu-rt-58 scheduled preemptible-terminate in ~12s (preemptible notice). Reason: cloud-spot-preempt.

Alex: What about streaming cutover? for streaming requests we should allow streaming to finish if >90% of tokens done; otherwise handoff and resume. We need a simple heuristic: if client saw last N tokens < 8, allow streaming to finish; else produce resume token.

Priya: cost question — holding redis entries for every mid-flight request could add up. Estimate: 500 concurrent preemptible connections * average 1 key per conn * 30s TTL = 500 keys * 30s churn. That seems fine, but we should track RPS and cache pressure.

Maria: telemetry: emit a short metric per handoff: runtime.evict.handoff.{success|miss|requeue_attempts} and histograms for requeue latency and duplicate-token suppression counts. Add a label for pool-type (preemptible vs reserved).

Shane: failure modes: token missing -> broker fallback to idempotent replay path (restarting request from model start) and mark as duplicated work. We'll add a circuit-breaker: if >5% of requeues in a minute caused full-replay, switch to conservative behaviour (increase drain to 20s or degrade to reserved pool).

Alex: quick config snippet for the broker I sketched: ```yaml
broker:
  requeue_attempts: 3
  base_backoff_ms: 150
  max_backoff_ms: 2000
  resume_token_ttl_s: 30
  drain_window_s: 10
  duplicate_suppression_window_ms: 500
```

Priya: One more thing — security. Make sure resume tokens are scoped to customer org so we don't leak cross-tenant references. HMAC key rotation needs to be safe.

Maria: Ops runbook note: when we see a spike in evict.handoff.miss, oncall should check redis eviction rate and cloud preemptible churn and consider temporarily pinning hot customers to reserved pools. Documented.

Shane: Action items: (1) Alex + Maria draft PR for broker + token schema (2) Priya to run perf sims for redis key pressure (3) I will add the metrics. We'll aim for a Canary on a small preemptible fleet next week. :thumbsup:

Priya: ack. I'll add a quick load test scenario to perf harness.

Alex: pulling a branch today.

Maria: adding dashboards + alerts.

Shane: cool. If no objections I'll fold into runtime-evict-sprint ticket and assign owners. Thanks everyone.
